outcome: Clinical characteristics (sex ratio, prenatal diagnosis, age of diagnosis, vomiting, misdiagnosis, cyst size, cyst fluid)
cohort: The study included 148 children with mesenteric lymphatic malformations and 53 children with omental lymphatic malformations who underwent surgical treatment at two centers in China between January 2016 and December 2022.
finding: There were significant differences in clinical characteristics, cyst characteristics, and preoperative complications between children with mesenteric lymphatic malformations and those with omental lymphatic malformations, with OL patients having larger cysts, more turbid fluid, and more preoperative complications but potentially better prognosis with laparoscopic surgery.
